newsitem.title: HAITI: Haitian president to marry in private ceremony.
newsitem.headline: Haitian president to marry in private ceremony.

text.p: President Rene Preval was set to marry Guerda Benoit, an employee of the Haitian foreign affairs ministry, in a private ceremony on Saturday at the National Palace.
"I'm very excited but I'm frantic, really," Benoit told Reuters as she made last-minute preparations on Friday.

Only 15 people, including Preval's two children from a previous marriage and Benoit's immediate family, were to attend the Roman Catholic ceremony. Benoit's cousin, Father Etienne Belneau, was expected to perform the ceremony.
Haiti's cabinet of ministers and even Preval's closest advisers were not invited to the wedding, according to palace officials.
Preval's predecessor, Jean-Bertrand Aristide, also wed in office, marrying New York lawyer Mildred Trouillot in January 1996, a couple of weeks before his term as president ended.

Preval was inaugurated in February 1996 in the first transfer of power from one democratically elected government to another in Haiti, a country with a long history of dictatorship and political chaos.
Preval and Benoit met in Washington, D.C. when then-Prime Minister Preval was living in the United States in exile after a 1991 military coup.
At the time, Benoit, currently an assistant delegate to the Organisation of American States, was working at the Haitian Embassy in Washington. She also once worked in the fashion industry.
Rumours circulated in recent months that Benoit, who has been living at the palace, and Preval had already married in a secret ceremony.
Preval, who described himself in a recent interview with Reuters as an ordinary man with extraordinary responsibilities, has taken on a low profile in recent weeks.
Haiti is in the throes of political crisis after the resignation of its prime minister a month ago, and economic crisis as Preval tries to push a controversial privatisation plan.
